conviction_note: Sum of four sized findings (-1.8, -0.9, -0.8, +1.2) = -2.3; the core is that Kroger's own quarterly EPS bridge makes the reaffirmed $5.10-$5.30 FY guide require an H2 operating-profit inflection just as the buyback lever that carried Q1 EPS collapsed to $198m, partly offset by grocery dollar inflation running ~55bp hotter in the Q2 window than the guide assumed; sized well inside the 5.95% implied move because this is a $35bn name with forty analysts and a stock already 24.7% off its high.

findings.finding: Kroger bought back only $198m of stock (3m shares) in Q1 2026 against a $2.0bn authorization it says in the same 10-Q it 'expects to complete by the end of fiscal 2026' — a 10%-of-plan pace — while the reaffirmed FY guide of $5.10-$5.30 needs H2 EPS of $2.48-$2.68 against $2.32 last year (+7% to +16%) with the y/y share-count tailwind decaying from -7.4% in Q1 (615m vs 664m diluted) toward ~-3% by Q4 as the FY2025 ASR laps out.
findings.why_not_priced: The buyback line was never raised on the Q1 call (the transcript contains no management discussion of repurchases at all) and no wire preview mentions it; the previews are anchored on the $1.05 consensus, which management itself pre-guided ('adjusted EPS in line with last year in the second quarter'), so the consensus number carries zero information and the real question — whether the FY range survives an H1 in which adjusted FIFO operating profit grew 1.7% (Q1 $1,544m vs $1,518m) and Q2 EPS is guided flat on a ~6% smaller share count, i.e. adjusted net earnings down ~6% — is not in the coverage. If it were priced, the 25-delta skew would not be -2.76 vol points with calls bid into a guidance-setting print; a market expecting the FY range to be cut pays for puts.
findings.independence: Two documents from the same issuer support one finding and the scorer should treat them as one cluster: the Q1 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926075395/tm2618219d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-06-18, Q1 adj FIFO OP $1,544m vs $1,518m, 615m vs 664m diluted, guidance reaffirmed) and the FY2025 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926023800/tm267907d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-03-05, FY2025 adj EPS $4.85, adj FIFO OP $4.9bn, 655m avg diluted, FY2026 guide incl. ~130bp IRA headwind). Genuinely independent corroboration that H2 is the swing factor: Kroger separately committed $1.25bn of cash to the Giant Eagle acquisition on 2026-07-01, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926079552/tm2619434d1_8k.htm.

findings.finding: Greg Foran (CEO since 2026-02-09, ex-Walmart U.S. CEO) has his hand-picked operating team landing in the two weeks straddling this print: Nate Faust as EVP/Chief eCommerce Officer effective 2026-09-01 (announced 08-11) and Mark Ibbotson as EVP/Chief Store Operations Officer effective 2026-09-14 (8-K filed 09-02, three days before the quiet period, on a $1m salary plus $3.5m of sign-on equity), both ex-Walmart/Asda.
findings.why_not_priced: A $1m-salary EVP appointment in a routine item-5.02 8-K nine days before a print draws no wire coverage and no analyst note — I found no sell-side commentary linking it to the quarter. The mechanism the market is missing is timing, not the person: Foran's documented Walmart playbook is price investment funded by cost-out with near-term margin sacrifice, he has already said publicly he will cut prices broadly and double new-store openings to 70-80 next year, and a CEO does not import a Chief Store Operations Officer to keep executing an inherited plan. Guidance resets are overwhelmingly delivered once the new team is seated. If the market had focused on this, the print would carry a visible 'reset risk' premium in put skew rather than the -2.76 call-bid skew actually quoted.
findings.independence: Separate source, separate document: Kroger's own release naming Faust, https://ir.kroger.com/news/news-details/2026/Kroger-names-Nate-Faust-Executive-Vice-President-and-Chief-eCommerce-Officer/default.aspx (2026-08-11). Foran's appointment and Walmart record: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926012061/tm265602d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-02-09). This rests on different documents from finding 1 and a different mechanism (management intent vs arithmetic), but both point at the same event — a Q2 guidance reset — so a scorer should not read them as two independent probabilities of that event.

findings.finding: The two peer prints that actually overlap Kroger's Q2 window (2026-05-24 to 2026-08-15) show the traffic going to mass and club, not to conventional supermarkets: Walmart U.S. comped +2.6% for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 led by transactions and RAISED FY27 guidance, and Costco's U.S. comp ex-gasoline and FX was +5.6% for the four weeks ended 2026-08-30 — against Kroger's own guide of identical sales 'roughly in line with the first quarter' at 1.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: The read-across note the street actually wrote was on 2026-07-23, off Albertsons' guidance cut, and Albertsons' quarter ended 2026-06-20 — it covers only the first four weeks of Kroger's Q2 and says nothing about July or August. Walmart's May-July quarter and Costco's August month are the only public reads on the back two-thirds of Kroger's quarter, and nobody re-ran the read-across on them because Walmart's print was framed as a Walmart story (tariff refunds, e-commerce, guidance raise). The distinction matters directionally: a soft-industry quarter is forgivable and a share-loss quarter is not, and share loss is what forces a price-investment reset. Had this been priced, Kroger would not be flat (+1.5%) over 20 days while Walmart raised guidance in the middle of that window.
findings.independence: Costco, a different company and filing: https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-August-Sales-Results/default.aspx (released 2026-09-02, four weeks ended 2026-08-30). Also, Ahold Delhaize's U.S. comp ex-gasoline was only +0.8% for its Q2, with the drags quantified as -0.9pp SNAP and egg deflation and -0.7pp IRA pharmacy pricing: https://newsroom.aholddelhaize.com/ahold-delhaize-reports-resilient-q2-2026-results-and-reiterates-guidance-for-the-year/ (2026-08-05) — i.e. conventional U.S. supermarkets ran near zero in the same window Walmart ran +2.6%.

findings.finding: Grocery dollar inflation is running materially hotter in Kroger's Q2 window than in the Q1 window that management extrapolated from: food-at-home CPI was +1.9% y/y in March 2026 but +2.7% y/y in each of May, June and July 2026, so Kroger's 'roughly in line with the first quarter' 1.0% identical-sales guide, set on 2026-06-18, embeds roughly 50-60bp less price than the quarter is actually carrying.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the one leg that cuts upward and it is the reason the answer is -2.3 and not -4. It is public and free, but the previews all quote the EPS consensus rather than the comp, and Kroger's identical-sales line is the number this stock trades on. Management guided the comp on 2026-06-18 with only March and April CPI in hand; June and July food-at-home prints (both +2.7%) landed after. Two of the eight prints in the reaction history were up 5%+ on a comp beat, so a 150-160bp comp against a 100bp guide is a real upside path that the -2.76 call-bid skew is arguably already leaning toward — which is exactly why I am sizing it as a partial offset rather than the headline.
findings.independence: USDA ERS confirms the July figure independently of the BLS TED article: 'food-at-home CPI was unchanged from June 2026 to July 2026 and 2.7 percent higher than in July 2025', https://ers.usda.gov/data-products/food-price-outlook/summary-findings. Corroborating that the price is showing up at conventional supermarket registers: Weis Markets comped +2.3% for the 13 weeks ended 2026-06-27 despite a ~$18.2m IRA pharmacy revenue drag, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000105418/000010541826000048/wmk-20260804xex99d1.htm (2026-08-04).

searched_and_found_nothing: Form 4 cluster of 13 filings on 2026-07-14/16 — read two of them, they are code-F tax withholding on restricted stock vesting (e.g. Carin Fike, 56 shares at $56.56); only one genuine open-market sale (Yael Cosset, 30,000 shares for $1.764m on 07-14), not a signal
UFCW labour action — the King Soopers/Local 7 strike material is all February 2025 and the SoCal tentative agreements are 2025; found no 2026 strike or contract expiry inside or after the quarter
Kroger layoffs/store closures — the '1,000 corporate layoffs' and '60 store closures' stories date to August 2025 under interim CEO Ron Sargent, relabelled by search as 2026; discarded on date

SNAP as a fresh negative — national participation fell to 36.6m in May 2026 from 42.2m in May 2025 (foodtradenews 2026-08-27), but May 2026 is inside Kroger's Q1, so the y/y drag is already in the +1.0% Q1 comp and in the reaffirmed guide; management named it on the Q1 call ('most impacted across three states'). Not incremental.

IRA Medicare maximum-fair-price pharmacy headwind — real and quantified at peers (Ahold -0.7pp, Weis ~$18.2m, Walmart -80bp), but Kroger disclosed ~130bp of it inside FY2026 guidance in the 2026-03-05 release, so it is explicitly priced
Giant Eagle antitrust/deal risk — announced 2026-07-01, closes 2027, fully covered; leverage at 1.75x vs a 2.3-2.5x target means the $1.25bn cash does not force a buyback trade-off
Kroger IR news-release index page and the Q4 2025 IR permalink both returned HTTP 404; used the SEC 8-K exhibits instead
Searched for a Kroger-specific operational event in the quarter (outage, recall, cyber, pricing-page or membership change) and found nothing dated inside 2026-05-24 to 2026-08-15
baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline: the 25-delta skew is -2.76 vol points with calls bid and the 20-day run-in is a flat +1.5%, i.e. the option market is leaning toward a bounce off a stock 24.7% below its high, while the guidance arithmetic in Kroger's own 10-Q and Q1 release plus the Walmart/Costco share reads point to the FY range being narrowed or trimmed — the one leg that agrees with the skew is the food-at-home inflation tailwind, which is why the net is only -2.3 rather than deeply negative.
